extracted.intended_audience: graduate students or advanced undergraduates studying algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, theorems, and exercises establishing dimension and codimension for topological spaces, rings, schemes, and varieties (Krull dimension, codimension/height, Noether normalization, dimension=transcendence degree, Going-Up/Down, semicontinuity, etc.). Useful for understanding and computing dimensions in algebraic geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of dimension (topological/Krull)
rubrics_metrics.description: The dimension of a topological space X (denoted dim X) is the supremum of lengths of chains of closed irreducible sets, indexing starting at 0 (may be infinite). The dimension of a ring is the supremum of lengths of chains of nested prime ideals (indexing starts at 0). These two definitions are sometimes called Krull dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholars of the empty set may take dim(empty) = −∞. The definition is purely topological (depends only on the topological space, not the structure sheaf). Example: compute dim Spec A = dim A. Note: over C algebraic dimensions are half the real picture (complex vs real intuition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality dim Spec A = dim A
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring A, dim Spec A equals the Krull dimension of A (supremum of lengths of chains of prime ideals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the bijection between irreducible closed subsets of Spec A and prime ideals of A (inclusion-reversing). Also dim Spec A = dim Spec A/N(A) because the Zariski topology disregards nilpotents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation examples for basic rings/schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: dim A1_k = 1, dim Spec Z = 1, dim Spec k = 0, dim Spec k[x]/(x^2) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify prime ideals explicitly (e.g., for k[t]: (0) and (f(t)) for irreducible f) and compute maximal chain lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension of reducible spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: If Z is the union of two closed subsets X and Y, then dim Z = max(dim X, dim Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dimension is not a local characteristic; prefer discussing dimensions of irreducible spaces. Define equidimensional/pure dimension: all irreducible components have the same dimension (pure dimension n). Terminology: equidimensional dimension 1 = curve, 2 = surface, n = n-fold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine-local criterion for scheme dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme has dimension n iff it admits an open cover by affine open subsets of dimension at most n, with equality achieved on some affine open subset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful reduction: bijection between irreducible closed subsets of an open U and those of X meeting U.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherian scheme of dimension 0 has finitely many points
rubrics_metrics.description: A Noetherian scheme of dimension 0 has a finite number of points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise-level fact; consequence of Noetherian hypotheses and structure of prime ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surjection of integral domains of same dimension is isomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: A surjection of integral domains of the same dimension must be an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise statement: use dimensions and properties of integral domains to deduce injectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fibers of integral morphisms have dimension 0
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is an integral morphism, then every nonempty fiber of π has dimension 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof outline: base change preserves integral morphisms; reduce to Y = Spec k and show finitely generated integral k-algebra that is integral over k has dim 0 (every nonzero element invertible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral extensions preserve dimension (Going-Up/Down input)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Spec B corresponds to an integral extension of rings A → B, then dim Spec A = dim Spec B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Going-Up Theorem to lift chains of primes and exercises to show chains upstairs and downstairs correspond; argue no two elements upstairs map to same downstairs element in a maximal chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization preserves dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: If ν : X' → X is the normalization (possibly in a finite extension of the function field), then dim X' = dim X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may assume X integral for convenience; normalization is integral over X, so use integral-extension dimension preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field extension preserves pure dimension for finite-type affine schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is an affine k-scheme of pure dimension n and K/k is an algebraic field extension, then XK := X ×_k K has pure dimension n; conversely, if XK has pure dimension n then X has pure dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to A integral domain; minimal primes of A⊗kK correspond to components. Use freeness of AK as A-module and previous dimension-preserving exercises. See Exercise 12.1.H and generalizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example computation: dim Z[x] = 2
rubrics_metrics.description: The ring Z[x] has Krull dimension 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: prime ideals of Z[x] were studied earlier; construct chain of primes of length 2 (e.g., (0) ⊂ (p) ⊂ (p, f(x)) etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of codimension (for irreducible Y in X)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is an irreducible closed subset of X, codim_X Y is the supremum of lengths of increasing chains of irreducible closed subsets starting with Y (indexing at 0). For a prime ideal p in a ring, its codimension (height) is the supremum of lengths of chains of decreasing prime ideals starting at p. codim p = dim A_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid defining codimension as dim X − dim Y in general (pathological for reducible spaces). The codimension of a point is the codimension of its closure. This definition aligns with linear-algebra codimension analogies and with localizing at primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codimension 0 and 1, and hypersurfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Y is codimension 0 in X iff Y is an irreducible component of X. Y is codimension 1 if for every irreducible component Y' containing it there is no irreducible closed subset strictly between Y and Y'. A closed subset whose irreducible components are all codimension 1 in X is a hypersurface in X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful: 'hypersurface' has slightly different meanings in different contexts (see Def. 9.3.2). Use examples and Figure 12.1 for intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: General inequality codim_X Y + dim Y ≤ dim X
rubrics_metrics.description: For Y an irreducible closed subset of scheme X, codim_X Y + dim Y ≤ dim X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equality need not hold in full generality (pathologies exist), but equality does hold for irreducible varieties (Theorem 12.2.9). See exercises and counterexamples in the text for nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codimension-one primes in UFDs are principal
rubrics_metrics.description: In a unique factorization domain A, all codimension 1 prime ideals are principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: pick nonzero f in p, take irreducible factor g in p; (g) is nonzero prime contained in p, and codim 1 forces equality p = (g). The converse holds under Noetherian hypothesis (see later Proposition 12.3.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of Noetherian local rings of dimension 0 (Artinian)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Noetherian local ring (A,m), the following are equivalent: (i) dim A = 0; (ii) m = N(A) (nilradical); (iii) for some n > 1, m^n = 0; (iv) A has finite length; (v) every descending sequence of ideals is eventually constant. Such a ring is called Artinian or finite length local ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise-level equivalences; shows dimension-zero local rings have strong finiteness properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of infinite-dimensional Noetherian rings (Nagata counterexample)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible for a Noetherian ring to have infinite Krull dimension; Nagata provides a construction showing this pathology (e.g., localize k[x1,x2,...] at a suitable multiplicative set).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 12.1.M outlines constructing S^{-1}A with arbitrarily long prime chains and proving S^{-1}A is Noetherian via a finiteness lemma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension = transcendence degree for finitely generated domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 12.2.1: If A is a finitely generated domain over a field k, then dim Spec A = trdeg K(A)/k. Hence if X is an irreducible k-variety then dim X = trdeg K(X)/k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: dim A^n = n (though proof uses the same machinery), dimension of an irreducible k-variety equals transcendence degree of its function field, and Nullstellensatz can be deduced. Proof uses Noether normalization and induction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of a rational map of irreducible varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X ⇢ Y is a dominant rational map of irreducible k-varieties of the same dimension, the degree of the rational map is the degree of the induced field extension; extend to reducible by summing degrees on components; degree is 0 if map is not dominant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree is multiplicative under composition: deg(ρ ∘ π) = deg(ρ) deg(π). Will be interpreted geometrically as counting preimages of general points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noether Normalization Lemma
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is an integral domain, finitely generated over a field k, and trdeg K(A)/k = n, then there are elements x1,...,xn ∈ A algebraically independent over k such that A is a finite (hence integral) extension of k[x1,...,xn].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric content: any integral finite-type affine k-scheme X admits a surjective finite morphism to A^n_k where n = trdeg K(X)/k. See projective version and exercises for refinements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nagata's proof idea (jiggling variables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nagata's trick: replace generators yi by zi = yi − y_m^{r_i} with carefully chosen exponents r_i so that an algebraic dependence isolates y_m as integral over the subring, producing a finite extension by induction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric intuition: choose a general projection to a hyperplane; non-finiteness occurs only in finitely many directions; 'jiggle' variables to avoid bad directions. Over infinite fields linear substitutions suffice for general choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additivity of dimension for products (finite-type hypothesis)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are irreducible finite-type k-varieties, then dim(X ×_k Y) = dim X + dim Y. In particular dim A[x] = dim A + 1 for A finitely generated over a field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: use surjective finite morphisms from X and Y to affine spaces and form product to get surjective finite morphism from X×Y to appropriate affine space. Warning: finite-type hypothesis is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codimension equals difference of dimensions for irreducible varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: For a pure-dimensional k-scheme X locally of finite type and irreducible closed Y with generic point η, dim Y + dim O_{X,η} = dim X; equivalently dim Y + codim_X Y = dim X (inequality (12.1.5.1) becomes equality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Noether normalization and the Going-Down Theorem for finite extensions of integrally closed domains; reduce to showing maximal proper closed irreducible subsets drop dimension by 1 (hypersurfaces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Catenary rings and chains of primes
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring A is catenary if for every nested pair of prime ideals p ⊂ q, all maximal chains of primes between p and q have the same length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localizations of finitely generated rings over a field are catenary; most naturally arising rings in algebraic geometry are catenary (examples: localizations of finitely generated Z-algebras, complete Noetherian local rings, Dedekind domains, Cohen–Macaulay rings). Noncatenary examples are rare and subtle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Going-Down Theorem for finite extensions of integrally closed domains
rubrics_metrics.description: If φ : B → A is a finite extension of rings with B an integrally closed domain and A an integral domain, and given primes q ⊂ q' of B and a prime p' of A lying over q', there exists a prime p ⊂ p' of A lying over q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric picture: chains of primes descend along finite integral extensions under integrally closed hypothesis. Proof uses normal closure, integral closure, Lying Over and Going-Up, and Galois automorphisms to move primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime avoidance proposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If p1,...,pn are prime ideals of A and I is an ideal not contained in any pi, then there exists f ∈ I not contained in any pi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret geometrically as existence of a function vanishing on none of the finitely many closed subsets; used in arguments like constructing elements avoiding a finite set of primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitivity of Galois automorphisms on primes in integral closure
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is integrally closed, L/K(B) a finite normal field extension, and C the integral closure of B in L, then automorphisms of L/K(B) act transitively on primes of C lying over a given prime q' of B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the proof of the Going-Down Theorem: conjugate primes and use norm/prime-avoidance arguments to force desired prime positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension at a point and upper semicontinuity
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Noetherian scheme X, define dim_X(p) as the dimension of the largest irreducible component of X containing p. Then dim_X(·) is an upper-semicontinuous function on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upper-semicontinuity informally means dimension can 'jump up' in limits; many geometric invariants (fiber dimension, rank of sheaves, degree of finite morphism) are semicontinuous (mostly upper), with some lower-semicontinuous exceptions (e.g., rank of a matrix of functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of local invariants at closed points (finite-type k-schemes)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p is a closed point of a locally finite-type k-scheme X, then three integers coincide: (i) dim_X p; (ii) dim O_{X,p}; and (iii) codim_X p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies geometric, local, and codimension notions of 'dimension at a point' in the finite-type setting (Exercise 12.2.L).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension preserved by field extension for finite-type schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a locally finite-type k-scheme of pure dimension n and K/k is any field extension, then X_K = X ×_k K has pure dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to affine integral case, decompose K as algebraic extension of purely transcendental extension, use Exercise 12.1.H and transcendence-basis arguments. Warning: finite-type hypothesis is necessary (counterexamples exist otherwise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of incidence correspondences for dimension counting (applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove statements like 'most degree d hypersurfaces in P^3 contain no lines', construct an incidence variety parametrizing pairs (line, hypersurface) and compare dimensions to show image lies in a proper closed subset of parameter space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute dimensions of parameter spaces (e.g., Grassmannian dimension, number of coefficients of degree-d polynomials up to scale) and deduce generic statements by dimension count; generalizes to Noether-Lefschetz and related results.
